In the left figure, on a table is placed a vertical gray rectangular-prism wooden block, and on the ground beside the table is placed another identical wooden block but laid horizontally; the vertical distance marked r indicates the height difference between the top of the vertical wooden block on the tabletop and the top of the horizontally placed wooden block on the ground. In the left figure, the height of the top of the vertical wooden block on the tabletop is h + L, and the height of the top of the horizontally placed wooden block on the ground is W, so r = (h + L) - W = 32. In the right figure, the height of the top of the horizontally placed wooden block on the tabletop is h + W, and the height of the top of the vertical wooden block on the ground is L, so s = (h + W) - L = 28. Adding the two equations gives r + s = 2h, therefore 32 + 28 = 2h, h = 30. Therefore the table is 30 inches high.

method.method_draft: Describe the image first: Figure 1 shows one identical rectangular wood block standing upright on the tabletop and the other lying flat on the floor beside the table; the marked length r is the vertical distance from the top of the upright tabletop block to the top of the flat floor block. Let the table height be h, the long side of a block be L, and the short side be W. From Figure 1, r=(h+L)-W=32. From Figure 2, s=(h+W)-L=28. Add the two equations to cancel L and W: r+s=2h, so h=(32+28)/2=30 inches.
